summary:
The Pitcairn Islands stand under the United Kingdom framework: defence, external affairs and military service are reserved to the United Kingdom, while domestic matters including criminal and family law are governed by local ordinance.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2001, so a visitor faces no criminalisation exposure on that ground under local law.

The Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and has been in force since 2010. The guarantee is constitutional rather than an offence provision, and it names sexual orientation and not gender identity, so a trans visitor has no express constitutional protection on gender-identity grounds.

The Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 defines marriage as the union of two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity, and same-sex marriage has been legal since 14 May 2015. The ordinance was unanimously approved by the Island Council on 1 April 2015, signed by Governor Jonathan Sinclair on 5 May 2015 and published on 13 May 2015. It also recognises civil partnerships performed outside Pitcairn, so a trans visitor's relationship is covered by the local recognition rules.

No trans-specific violence incident, targeted screening practice, facilities rule, healthcare restriction or hate-crime case is documented for the Pitcairn Islands in these sources, and no enforcement record of the constitutional non-discrimination guarantee is sourced.
tangentialFactors:
The population is roughly 50 residents, and none is known to be in a same-sex relationship, which limits the local evidence base on how the non-discrimination guarantee operates in practice.

The sources are republications of encyclopedia entries rather than government or court documents, so the legal dates and ordinance provisions they carry are consistent across them but unverified against the published ordinance text in this record.
localsOnly:
Adoption has been legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2015 and is open to married, unmarried and single people.

The Island Council approved the Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 unanimously on 1 April 2015, after which the Governor signed it on 5 May 2015 and it was published on 13 May 2015.

The constitutional non-discrimination guarantee binds public authorities through the Constitution Order rather than creating a criminal offence, so remedies run through constitutional rather than criminal channels.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the constitutional prohibition on discrimination based on sexual orientation has been invoked, adjudicated or enforced is unresolved in this record; no case, complaint or official guidance is sourced.

Gender-identity-specific protection, legal gender recognition, and any local rule on identity documents or markers are not sourced for the Pitcairn Islands and remain unresolved here.

Practical matters for a visitor, including screening at the point of entry, access to gender-affirming care, and facility use, are not sourced for this jurisdiction; the sources address statutory rights only.

The claim that none of the roughly 50 residents is known to be in a same-sex relationship is undated in the sources, so its currency is unresolved.
